label: takeback
context: The 'takeback' project aims to provide chess players with a unique tool for analyzing their past games by allowing them to replay blunders against an AI clone of their opponent. This innovative application addresses the common frustration of recognizing missed opportunities in chess games, offering a second chance to correct mistakes and improve gameplay. The system's architecture is a blend of frontend and backend components, leveraging TypeScript and Svelte for a responsive and user-friendly interface, while the backend is built with FastAPI and Python. The core functionality revolves around ingesting chess game data from Chess.com, processing it, and training a custom-built MLP (Multilayer Perceptron) model to mimic the user's playing style. This clone model then serves as the opponent in a replay scenario, providing personalized feedback and analysis. The data flow begins with a user connecting their Chess.com account, triggering the training of a clone model based on their game history. The model learns from snapshots of each move, considering board positions, player timing, and move probabilities, ultimately capturing the user's tendencies and chess persona over hundreds of games. The trained model is then used to simulate games, allowing users to replay their moves and receive commentary from a language model (Gemma). The application is containerized using Docker, enabling easy deployment and reproducibility. The team, consisting of three members, achieved a significant accomplishment by creating a clone model that outperformed the baseline Maia model with approximately 60% accuracy, demonstrating the effectiveness of their custom MLP architecture. The project utilizes a SQLite database for local storage and a PostgreSQL database for more robust data management, and integrates Stockfish for chess engine functionality. The codebase, comprising 106 source files, showcases a well-structured approach to development, with separate modules for analysis, model training, and user interface components. The project's success lies in its ability to combine advanced AI techniques with a practical application, providing chess players with a valuable tool for self-improvement and a unique perspective on their gameplay.
